Floodwaters rose in Taal, Bangkal, Davao City following the heavy rainfall on the evening of July 24, 2026. Several residents have already been rescued and safely evacuated. But every time I see scenes like this, I can't help but think about the ones who cannot ask for help, the strays still searching for dry ground, and the pets I hope were not left behind. If I had one wish, it would be for every kind family, every innocent soul, every beloved pet, and every homeless stray to be kept safe from the flood. And if it must reach somewhere, let it expose the places that have shown cruelty instead, like the impounding facilities where animals are neglected, the establishments that drive away hungry strays, and the homes of owners who abandoned or abused the lives they chose to keep. Because the voiceless deserve mercy. Cruelty does not. My heart is with everyone affected today, especially the voiceless. Olongapo City, Zambales  is facing widespread flooding as persistent Southwest Monsoon, or Habagat, rains continue to swell rivers and waterways across the city. According to The Philippine Daily Inquirer, floodwaters overflowed the Sta. Rita and Del Rosario bridges, affecting parts of Sta. Rita, West Bajac-Bajac, East Bajac-Bajac and Kalaklan, while several major roads became impassable. The situation became more serious on August 29, when the Olongapo City Information Center, cited by Inquirer, reported that 1,395 people from 452 families were already staying in evacuation centers, with other residents seeking shelter outside designated facilities. Some communities experienced waist- to neck-deep flooding, while rescue teams were deployed to assist stranded residents. The flooding was driven by continuous monsoon rains, with PAGASA placing Zambales under a Red Rainfall Warning, meaning serious flooding was expected in flood-prone areas. Authorities continue to monitor river levels and conduct rescue and evacuation operations as rain persists. For many residents, familiar streets and neighborhoods have temporarily turned into waterways, forcing families to leave their homes and move toward safer ground. The situation remains dangerous, particularly near swollen rivers, bridges and rapidly flowing floodwater, and residents in vulnerable areas are being urged to follow evacuation orders and local disaster warnings. ITO ANG ISA SA MGA DAHILAN KUNG BAKIT BUMABAHA” — PANAWAGAN SA DISIPLINA SA BASURA Ipinunto ang problema sa basurang bumabara sa mga daluyan ng tubig bilang isa sa mga dahilan ng pagbaha. Ayon sa pahayag, kailangang linisin ng pamahalaan ang mga lugar na puno ng basura at gawin ang responsibilidad nito.  Ngunit hindi umano sapat ang paglilinis lamang kung patuloy ding bumabalik ang problema. Nanawagan din siya ng mas mahigpit na disiplina sa pagtatapon ng basura at hinikayat ang publiko na magmungkahi ng konkretong solusyon. Kabilang sa mga ideyang maaaring pag-usapan ang mas mahigpit na enforcement, mas mabigat na multa, CCTV monitoring, community accountability, at incentives para sa mga sumusunod sa tamang pagtatapon.  “Hindi puwedeng ganito na lang palagi.” #Baha #Basura #FloodControl #MMDA #Disiplina #NewsUpdate #Philippines See less ITO ANG ISA SA MGA DAHILAN KUNG BAKIT BUMABAHA” — PANAWAGAN SA DISIPLINA SA BASURA
